issues.description: default_raise sentinel and its comment still reference '< 3.10 compatibility' after dropping 3.9
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py keeps default_raise() with the comment 'just for < 3.10 compatibility' and the comment block above TransactionEndpointRequest referencing the same. Now that kw_only is universally available, field(default_factory=default_raise) for required kw-only fields is dead scaffolding; the literate explanation no longer matches the code. Either remove the sentinel and make these fields truly required (no default), or update the rationale.

issues.description: test-install-scripts.yml leaves diagnostic 'dnf search python3.12' in production CI shell
issues.detail: The Amazon and Rocky prep steps now run 'dnf update -y; dnf search python3.12; dnf install git python3.12 -y'. The search invocation is a debugging artifact: it produces noise, has no effect on the install, and 'dnf update -y' on every CI run is a heavy, unmotivated change from the prior minimal 'yum install --assumeyes git'. State why update is needed or drop it; remove the search.

issues.description: Ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 broadly disabled with a TODO instead of a tracked migration
issues.detail: The PR description promises Union/Optional rewrites, but ruff.toml globally ignores UP007, UP035, UP045 with only a 'TODO: Remove these' comment. This defers the stated rigor indefinitely with no issue link, no scope, and no kill-date. A reader cannot tell whether this is a 3% deferred optimization or permanent debt. Reference a tracking issue or stage the cleanup in this PR.

issues.description: install.sh version-range check still uses minor>=7 lower bound after raising floor to 3.10
issues.detail: The guard reads '[ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ] || [ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -ge "13" ]' while the error message says '>= 3.10 and < 3.13.0'. The bound and the message disagree: a system python 3.8 would pass the numeric check yet contradict the message. Tighten lower bound to 10 so code and documentation agree.

issues.description: conditions.py loses the literate comment explaining the pragma without explaining why it is now safe
issues.detail: Previously the 'continue' carried a multi-line comment about a 3.9 coverage quirk and a link to coveragepy#1530. The new code is just 'continue'. The reader of this branch will wonder why the else-branch exists at all. A one-line comment ('unhandled condition type; skip') preserves intent now that the coverage workaround is gone.

issues.description: itertools.pairwise substitution is correct but unaudited for empty input invariant
issues.detail: Replacing zip(ordered, ordered[1:]) with itertools.pairwise(ordered) is asymptotically and semantically equivalent on non-empty sequences and on empty input (both yield nothing). The change is fine, but no comment states the loop invariant 'every adjacent pair is ordered'. A one-line invariant comment would make sane() self-documenting; cheap rigor win.

review.summary: The 3.9-removal mechanics are largely sound: version pins, CI matrices, install scripts, and dataclass kw_only branches are consistently raised, and the itertools.pairwise swap is a clean semantic equivalent. Rigor gaps remain around literate hygiene — stale '< 3.10 compatibility' comments and the default_raise sentinel persist in wallet_request_types.py, and a coverage-quirk comment was removed without replacement context in conditions.py. The ruff.toml UP007/UP035/UP045 blanket ignore with a bare TODO defers the PR's stated Union→| migration with no tracking, which is exactly the kind of unmeasured deferred work Knuth flags. CI prep steps gained a debugging 'dnf search' and an unmotivated 'dnf update -y' that should be justified or removed. install.sh's numeric guard still allows 3.7–3.9 while the error message claims ≥3.10; align them. Overall: RIGOROUS on the version bump, NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the leftover scaffolding.
